title: Set x = rs("Name") binds x to the Field object; x = rs("Name") reads the default-property Value. Two characters of source change the semantic
sourceContent:
Attribute VB_Name = "modCustomers"
Option Explicit

' Two read paths that look almost identical but have different semantics.
' DefaultRead returns the Variant value (string contents of the Name field).
' SetRead returns a Field object reference whose downstream behaviour is
' UPDATE-tracked: assigning to fld.Value changes the row.
'
' Migration tools that translate both to `var x = rs.Fields["Name"];` lose
' the SET vs implicit distinction silently — the customer's bug surfaces
' only when the SetRead path is updated and re-saved.

Public Function DefaultRead(rs As DAO.Recordset) As String
    Dim x As Variant
    x = rs("Name")              ' x is the .Value (a String here)
    DefaultRead = CStr(x)
End Function

Public Function SetRead(rs As DAO.Recordset) As DAO.Field
    Dim fld As DAO.Field
    Set fld = rs("Name")        ' fld is the Field object reference
    Set SetRead = fld
End Function

canonicalInputs.rationale: Implicit access reads Value; returns the String contents.
Set binds x to the Field object; downstream code can mutate Value (and the recordset stays update-aware until rs.Update or rs.Edit/Update boundary).

notes: Set vs assignment is the most-missed VB6 distinction in any LLM-only port. Bang notation (rs!Name) also dispatches to the default property AND is interchangeable with rs("Name") on the read path — but SET against bang notation is rarely valid syntax. The extraction MUST emit two distinct default_property_usage claims (one per read path) and an open_question asking the SME whether the customer's downstream code relies on the Field-reference path being update-aware. Collapsing both paths into a single 'reads the Name field' claim is a calibration miss.
